Article Title: Neutron scans of a 100-million-year-old Queensland ichthyosaur found fish, cephalopods and a pterosaur in its stomach; crushing bite marks point to giant Kronosaurus
Article Text:
Representative Image (Canva)

Scans uncover the ichthyosaur's last meal

Fossilised stomach that was scanned (Image Credit: Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation)

Bite marks point to a fearsome marine predator

A rare glimpse into an ancient ecosystem

According to a study published in the journal Gondwana Research, supported by findings from the Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation (ANSTO), neutron and synchrotron scans of a 100-million-year-old ichthyosaur fossil from Queensland have uncovered the marine reptile's final meal, and clues to its violent end. Researchers found the remains of fish, cephalopods and part of a pterosaur preserved inside its stomach, while crushing bite marks suggest it was probably scavenged or attacked by the giant marine predator Kronosaurus queenslandicus. The fossil offers a rare glimpse into the complex food web of Australia's ancient inland sea.A remarkably preserved fossil from northwestern Queensland has allowed scientists to reconstruct one of the most dramatic prehistoric stories ever captured in stone. By combining advanced neutron imaging with high-resolution synchrotron X-ray scans, researchers were able to examine the fossil without damaging it, revealing both what the ancient predator had eaten and what likely happened to it shortly afterwards.The fossil belongs to a large ichthyosaur, a dolphin-shaped marine reptile that lived during the Early Cretaceous period around 100 million years ago. Measuring between six and seven metres in length, the animal swam through the vast Eromanga Sea, which once covered much of inland Australia and supported a rich diversity of marine life.The specimen, nicknamed "Bag of Bones" or "B.O.B.", was discovered in 2019 by fossil hunters at a public fossicking site near Richmond, Queensland. During its preparation, scientists noticed several rock nodules preserved behind the skull. Rather than opening them mechanically, they turned to neutron tomography and synchrotron computed tomography to investigate their contents.The scans revealed an extraordinary collection of remains inside the animal's stomach. Researchers identified bones belonging to fish and cephalopods, marine animals related to today's squid and cuttlefish. Even more remarkably, they also found fragments of a pterosaur jaw.The discovery marks the first direct fossil evidence anywhere in the world of an ichthyosaur consuming a pterosaur. Scientists suggest the ichthyosaur most likely seized the pterosaur while it was floating or skimming the water's surface, where pterosaurs often searched for fish, instead of hunting it in mid-air.The exceptionally preserved stomach contents provide a rare snapshot of the ichthyosaur's feeding behaviour and show that its diet was more varied than previously documented.While the stomach contents reveal the ichthyosaur's final meal, its skeleton tells another story. Researchers found extensive crushing damage across several bones, including massive bite marks indicating the animal was attacked or scavenged after death. The injuries were too severe to have resulted from normal decomposition or fossilisation.Based on the size and pattern of the bite marks, the research team believes the most likely predator was Kronosaurus queenslandicus, one of the largest marine reptiles ever to inhabit Australia's ancient seas. This enormous pliosaur possessed a massive skull and powerful jaws capable of crushing large prey with tremendous force.If this interpretation is correct, the fossil records a remarkable sequence. The ichthyosaur had recently eaten fish, cephalopods and a pterosaur before becoming the victim of an even larger apex predator.Complete stomach contents are rarely preserved in fossils, making discoveries like this exceptionally valuable. Even rarer are specimens that preserve evidence of both an animal's diet and the injuries that likely led to or followed its death.According to the researchers, the fossil provides one of the clearest pictures yet of the food web that existed in the Cretaceous Eromanga Sea. It shows that fish, cephalopods, flying reptiles and giant marine predators were all linked within a dynamic ecosystem where predators could quickly become prey.The discovery also demonstrates the growing importance of non-destructive imaging techniques in palaeontology. By using neutron and synchrotron scanning, scientists could examine structures hidden deep inside the fossil while leaving the specimen intact for future research.Beyond revealing the final moments of a single marine reptile, the Queensland ichthyosaur provides an extraordinary snapshot of life in Australia's ancient inland sea. From its diverse last meal to the crushing bite marks left by a giant predator, the fossil preserves a prehistoric food web frozen in time.
Article Summary: Fossil of a large ichthyosaur was found in northwestern Queensland. Researchers found the remains of fish, cephalopods and part of a pterosaur preserved inside its stomach. crushing bite marks suggest it was probably scavenged or attacked by the giant marine predator Kronosaurus queenslandicus. The fossil offers a rare glimpse into the complex food web of Australia's ancient inland sea.

Article Title: In 2000, an aquarium plant escaped into California waters; removing the ‘killer algae’ took six years and over $7 million
Article Text:
Caulerpa taxifolia, commonly known as “killer algae,” originates from the tropical waters of the Caribbean

The killer algae on the rise

Why it went so viral

One of the coolest things about Caulerpa taxifolia is how well it can reproduce

An ecological catastrophe

California’s costly fight

The eradication effort took six years, officially ending in 2006, at a cost of over US$7 million

Some of the biggest ecological disasters start in the least likely places. Here it may have started with a home aquarium. An online report by the Centre for Invasive Species Research states that an ornamental seaweed, Caulerpa taxifolia, escaped into the coastal waters of Southern California in 2000, likely after an aquarium owner illegally dumped marine plants into a stormwater system. What seemed to be an isolated incident quickly became an environmental emergency and a six-year eradication campaign costing over US$7 million. This is one of the most dramatic examples of how a non-threatening aquarium species can become a destructive invasive threat.For the uninitiated, Caulerpa taxifolia, commonly known as “killer algae,” originates from the tropical waters of the Caribbean, the Indian Ocean and parts of the Pacific. But its invasive story started in Europe. In the 1980s, aquarium managers at the Wilhelma Zoo in Stuttgart, Germany, bred a cold-tolerant strain for display tanks. In 1984, this modified strain had accidentally escaped to the Mediterranean Sea from the Oceanographic Museum of Monaco and soon covered thousands of hectares of the seabed. Unlike many marine plants, this strain grows in cooler waters, can survive out of water for up to 10 days in damp conditions and occurs in a range of underwater habitats including rocky reefs, sandy bottoms, mudflats and seagrass meadows.It was one of the world's most successful marine invaders, due to its remarkable adaptability.One of the coolest things about Caulerpa taxifolia is how well it can reproduce. The invasive strain reproduces by asexual fragmentation. Even the tiniest fragment, only one centimetre in size, can develop into a brand new plant. Fragments can be transported unwittingly long distances by ocean currents, boat anchors, fishing gear and ballast water from ships, allowing new colonies to quickly become established. Once established, this resilience makes the species particularly difficult to control.It is said that dense underwater meadows of the algae smother native seaweeds, seagrasses and marine invertebrates by blocking out sunlight and releasing toxic compounds known as caulerpenyne. This leads to less native habitat, which leads to fewer fish, which leads to less biodiversity and disrupts whole marine ecosystems. Some fish species that feed on the algae accumulate the toxins in their bodies, making them unfit for human consumption and threatening local fisheries. The expansion of Caulerpa has severely altered coastal ecosystems in some areas of the Mediterranean and has had consequences for commercially important fishing grounds.Authorities moved quickly after the algae was found first in California’s Agua Hedionda Lagoon near San Diego and later at Huntington Harbour near Los Angeles, states the report. Scientists covered the affected patches underwater with big tarpaulins, sealed them with sandbags and pumped chlorine underneath to kill off the infestation. The chlorine in the enclosure killed the algae but also killed fish, plants and other marine organisms trapped under the covers. The drastic intervention, while harsh on the environment, was thought to be the only realistic option to prevent the invasive species from spreading further up the California coast. The eradication effort took six years, officially ending in 2006, at a cost of over US$7 million, adds the report.Images Courtesy: istock
Article Summary: Caulerpa taxifolia escaped into the coastal waters of Southern California in 2000. It was likely after an aquarium owner illegally dumped marine plants into a stormwater system. The eradication effort took six years, officially ending in 2006, at a cost of over US$7 million.

Article Title: Japan earthquake aftermath: Woman dies of heat stroke in parked car; toll rises to 36
Article Text:
Workers inspect debris of the Kinparo inn, founded in 1910, for conservation of a possible rebuilding in Yatsushiro, southern Japan

An elderly woman apparently died of heat stroke while sheltering in her car, after the massive earthquake that killed over 30, as authorities warned of growing heat-related risks for evacuees amid sweltering temperatures.The woman, believed to be in her 70s, was found dead in a car on Thursday. NHK reported the vehicle had run out of fuel, preventing the use of air conditioning. Officials said the death was linked to the extreme heat that has gripped the quake-hit region."It's heartbreaking," Kumamoto Governor Takashi Kimura said, urging evacuees staying in vehicles to keep enough fuel to run air conditioning or move to air-conditioned evacuation centres.The magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture on Japan's southern main island of Kyushu on Tuesday, killing at least 36 people and injuring 105 others. Authorities are also investigating two additional deaths to determine whether they were quake-related.The disaster has left thousands displaced, with more than 9,000 people staying in schools, community centres and other emergency shelters, while many others continue to sleep in cars or outside their homes for privacy.The Japan Meteorological Agency said temperatures in Kumamoto city reached 36.6 degrees Celsius on Saturday and could climb even higher, raising fears of further heat-related illnesses.Authorities have begun distributing leaflets urging evacuees sheltering in vehicles to stay hydrated, move to cooler locations where possible and exercise regularly to reduce the risk of blood clots.Nearly 47,000 households remain without fresh water, while fuel shortages have led to long queues at petrol stations as supplies gradually resume.Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said the government was rushing water, food, portable toilets, air conditioners and partitions to evacuation centres to improve living conditions."The government is determined to do everything we can," Takaichi said.Search and recovery operations continued across the prefecture, with thousands of Self Defense Forces personnel, police officers, rescue workers and sniffer dogs deployed.Authorities on Saturday concluded a days-long operation at an Aeon Mall in Kashima, one of the worst-hit sites, where five survivors and the bodies of seven victims were recovered after a suspected gas explosion triggered by the earthquake caused part of the building to collapse.At another disaster site, a chimney collapsed at a Nippon Paper Industries factory in Yatsushiro city, killing nine workers. Two others were rescued.Officials said more than 180 homes had been destroyed and over 3,800 buildings damaged, while fewer than 900 households remained without electricity.
Article Summary: The woman, believed to be in her 70s, was found dead in a car on Thursday. The vehicle had run out of fuel, preventing the use of air conditioning. Officials said the death was linked to the extreme heat that has gripped the quake-hit region.

Article Title: Washington wildfires scorch over 2,50,000 acres; trigger mass evacuations
Article Text:
Old Trails Fire burns near Dwight Merkel Sports Complex (AP photo)

More than 4,000 firefighters, backed by the National Guard and crews from over a dozen states, battled multiple wildfires across Washington state, US on Saturday as strong winds and extreme heat fuelled blazes that forced widespread evacuations and power outages.Governor Bob Ferguson declared a statewide emergency and imposed a burn ban, warning that Washington was facing a "very serious situation" with more than a dozen active fires burning across over 250,000 acres. Nearly 450,000 acres have burned across the state so far this summer."Our state is facing a very serious situation with multiple fires," Ferguson said, adding that high temperatures and strong winds are expected to hamper firefighting efforts through the weekend.The biggest concern remained the fast-moving Old Trails Fire in Spokane, which erupted around noon, raced through dry brush and grass, jumped the Spokane River and spread into residential neighbourhoods.The blaze had burned about 3,000 acres by Saturday evening, threatened nearly 4,000 structures and forced evacuations across parts of the city. Cars lined roads as residents fled while thick smoke and towering flames engulfed the area."We urge residents of Spokane to heed evacuation orders and to stay alert to changing conditions and evacuations as they are rapidly changing," Courtney James, spokesperson for the Washington State Department of Natural Resources, said.Spokane Mayor Lisa Brown said around 200 homes had been evacuated by late afternoon, but warned the figure was likely to rise as evacuation zones expanded. Several major facilities, including water reclamation plants, a waste-to-energy facility and a Department of Veterans Affairs hospital, were also evacuated.Firefighters had achieved zero containment of the Old Trails Fire by Saturday evening, and officials said the cause remained under investigation. Authorities confirmed that some structures had been destroyed, though the full extent of the damage was still being assessed.Power utility Avista implemented public safety shutoffs amid the fire threat, leaving about 60,000 customers without electricity.State Forester George Geissler said the Spokane blaze was one of five major fire complexes burning across Washington. The largest, the Kaiser Canyon Fire in the state's northeast, had grown to about 134,000 acres."This is not normal... Throughout the state of Washington we're seeing fires raging," Public Lands Commissioner Dave Upthegrove said.No fire-related deaths or injuries had been reported as of Saturday evening."It's a tragedy what we're seeing over there," Major General Gent Welsh of the Washington National Guard said. "When the sun sets and the sun rises in the morning, I think we're going to be in shock to see some of the scenes that emerged out there."
Article Summary: More than 4,000 firefighters, backed by the National Guard and crews from over a dozen states, battled multiple wildfires across Washington state, US on Saturday. Governor Bob Ferguson declared a statewide emergency and imposed a burn ban, warning that Washington was facing a "very serious situation" with more than a dozen active fires burning across over 250,000 acres.

Article Title: Twitch streamer ExtraEmily gets her own Hulu and Disney+ series as Creator Essentials brings her Twitch content to TV
Article Text:
Image/Instagram

ExtraEmily:

Creator Essentials

.

Twitch streamer ExtraEmily gets her own Creator Essentials series

ExtraEmily: Creator Essentials

ExtraEmily expands from Twitch to major streaming platforms

ExtraEmily: Creator Essentials

With ExtraEmily: Creator Essentials

Twitch streamer ExtraEmily is taking her content from livestreams to television with her own series,The new show is part of a partnership between creator company pocket.watch and major streaming platforms. The series has 15 episodes, with each episode running for about 22 minutes. It is made for a teen audience and focuses on Emily’s fun personality, real-life challenges, gaming adventures and social experiments. The move gives ExtraEmily a new way to reach viewers beyond Twitch and puts her content alongside shows available on major streaming services.is built around the Twitch creator and her everyday adventures. Instead of simply showing clips from her livestreams, the series turns her content style into longer television episodes.The show has 15 episodes, with each one lasting around 22 minutes. The episodes are designed for teenagers and are part of pocket.watch’s growing creator-focused entertainment lineup.ExtraEmily is known for her IRL streams, gaming content and unpredictable livestreams. Her new series brings those ideas into a more structured TV format.The show includes different types of challenges and adventures. These can include real-life activities, social experiments and gaming speedruns. The goal is to keep the episodes fun and fast-moving while showing the personality that made ExtraEmily popular online.The series is also connected to a larger push by pocket.watch to bring digital creators to television and streaming platforms.The launch is an important step for ExtraEmily because most of her career has been built around livestreaming. Twitch allows creators to interact with viewers in real time, while a television series gives them a chance to reach people who may not follow them on livestream platforms.ExtraEmily is also part of Rabbit Hole, another pocket.watch creator series featuring a large group of internet creators. The show is available through Hulu and Disney+ and is aimed at younger viewers and teens.However,gives Emily a much bigger role because the series is centered around her.The project also shows how online creators are becoming a bigger part of traditional entertainment. Creators who first built audiences on Twitch, YouTube and other social platforms are now getting opportunities to make longer shows for major streaming services.For ExtraEmily, the series is another major step in her growing career. She can now take the style that made her popular on Twitch and bring it to a new audience through television-style episodes., the Twitch streamer is moving beyond livestreams and showing that internet creators can also become the stars of full-length streaming shows.
Article Summary: ExtraEmily is known for her IRL streams, gaming content and unpredictable livestreams. Her new series brings those ideas into a more structured TV format. The show has 15 episodes, with each one lasting around 22 minutes. The episodes are designed for teenagers and are part of pocket.watch’s growing creator- focused entertainment lineup.

Article Title: US: 3 killed in Idaho shopping area shooting; gunman among dead
Article Text:
This still image captured from video by a witness shows the scene of a shooting that started at an In-N-Out Burger restaurant

Three people were killed and at least two others injured after a gunman opened fire near an In-N-Out Burger restaurant in a busy shopping area in Twin Falls, Idaho, on Saturday, police said.The shooter was also among the dead, Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks said, adding that authorities were still working to identify the gunman and determine a motive, reported Reuters."We believe the threat to the community is over," Hicks told reporters. However, he said officials were still determining the exact number of people killed or injured and were in the process of notifying next of kin."It was a very chaotic scene," he added.The shooting was reported at around 2.30 pm local time near the popular restaurant in a high-traffic commercial district. About an hour later, authorities said the shooter was "no longer a threat."Twin Falls public information coordinator Josh Palmer confirmed to Reuters that three people had died and at least two others were injured and that the gunman was among those killed.The shooting unfolded near a busy shopping area crowded with people at the time.Police interviewed witnesses and urged anyone with information to contact investigators.Eyewitness Lane Koehn, 34, said he was stopped at a traffic light near the restaurant when he saw a person carrying an AR-style rifle emerge from the drive-thru. He said another man armed with a pistol began firing at the suspect.Koehn said he later saw an In-N-Out employee dragging a wounded co-worker, who had been shot in the chest, across the parking lot. "She was pretty bad off, but I don't know. I hope she made it," Koehn said.He added that police ordered people to evacuate as the shooting was still active and that it did not appear the gunman was targeting anyone in particular.Another witness, Haley Dodaro, who was waiting in the drive-thru with her mother, said they initially thought there had been a fire before realising there was an active shooter."So that's when we knew there was a shooting. People were running out crying and screaming. It was very scary," Dodaro told The Associated Press in a text message.Twin Falls County Commissioner Brent Reinke said Sheriff Jack Johnson initially informed him that five people had been hurt, though officials later said they were still verifying the casualty count.Authorities closed roads and a nearby bridge in the immediate aftermath of the shooting as multiple law enforcement agencies responded. St. Luke's Magic Valley medical centre said it was working closely with emergency responders.Twin Falls, a city of about 56,000 people, is located around 130 miles southeast of Boise in Idaho's Magic Valley region.
Article Summary: Gunman opened fire at In-N-Out Burger in Twin Falls, Idaho, on Saturday. Three people were killed and at least two others were injured, police said. The shooter was also among the dead, Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks said.

Article Title: Indian-origin mayor of US city asks ICE to 'go home', says he will always support the immigrant community
Article Text:
Indian-origin mayor of Connecticut's Norwich, Swarnjit Singh, said ICE is not welcome in their city.

Mayor Swarnjit Singh's strong statement on ICE

The mayor of Norwich, a city in Connecticut, issued a detailed statement condemning ICE activities around the city and asserting that the city administration will not support ICE. The Indian-origin mayor, Swarnjit Singh, is also the first Sikh mayor of the city and his support for the immigrants drew flak on social media, with many commenting that he should be deported first.In his statement, Singh said no one in Norwich should be afraid to go to work, send their children to school, or interact with our local police because of their immigration status. "I have always and will always support the immigrant community of Norwich," he said, adding that the Norwich Police Department (NPD) follows the CT Trust Act and they do not stop individuals because of their immigration status and do not assist or facilitate ICE enforcement."Following ICE’s recent activity in Norwich, I followed up with community leaders, local organizations, and state officials who work with these communities directly to reaffirm the City’s commitment to ensuring that all residents feel safe and supported, while coordinating the proper safety plans moving forward," Singh said in his statement."I want our immigrant communities to know that they are part of Norwich, and we will continue to listen, communicate, and work together to make sure people feel safe and supported.My position is the same as Governor Lamont’s, 'ICE, go home. You are not welcomed here'," his statement read.One social media handle noted that Singh himself was not born in America and came to the US as an international student in 2007. "A foreign-born man is now using his power and unconstitutional liberal "laws" to try and make sure federal agents cannot do their jobs in his city - despite the fact that federal law supersedes state law. This is not compassion. This is a middle finger to every citizen who follows the rules. He should be denaturalized and deported. It's time to pass a federal law that says foreign-born individuals cannot be elected to ANY office," the comment said.Singh recently received threats targeting him and his family, which the police defined as a hate crime.
Article Summary: Indian-origin mayor of Connecticut's Norwich, Swarnjit Singh, said ICE is not welcome in their city. Singh said no one in Norwich should be afraid to go to work, send their children to school, or interact with our local police because of their immigration status.

Article Title: Russia's overnight ballistic missile and drone attack on Ukraine capital Kyiv kills 9
Article Text:
Fire breaks out at Moscow's St Basil's Cathedral

At least nine people were killed and twenty-eight others were injured after Russia launched a barrage of ballistic missiles and drones targeting Ukraine's capital Kyiv overnight into Saturday. The attack damaged residential buildings, sparked multiple fires across the city and left people trapped under debris, officials said.Kyiv mayor Vitalii Klitschko had earlier said a five-storey residential building in the Solomianskyi district was struck by falling debris, causing severe damage and trapping residents inside."The first and second floors of the damaged residential building had partially collapsed," Klitschko said in a post on Telegram, adding that a fire had also broken out in the courtyard.Klitschko had said at least three people had been killed in the Russian missile attack and confirmed that several people remained trapped in the partially collapsed building. He added that five people had been hospitalised following the strikes.People were also believed to be trapped in another residential building in the Shevchenkivskyi district after the first and second floors partially collapsed, Klitschko said.Additionally, seven people were killed and 14 others injured in Kyiv's Darnytskyi district after the attack sparked fires and damaged homes, vehicles, an administrative building and other non-residential structures, emergency services told news agency AP.According to Reuters witnesses, more than a dozen explosions reverberated across the Ukrainian capital during the attack. This comes as Russia stepped up strikes on Kyiv in recent months, while Ukraine continues to face a shortage of air defence systems capable of intercepting ballistic missiles, which travel several times faster than the speed of sound.The latest bombardment came just two days after another large-scale Russian ballistic missile and drone attack across Ukraine killed 10 civilians and wounded more than 50 others. During that attack, a Russian missile also briefly entered Polish airspace.As Russian aerial attacks intensified, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy reiterated Kyiv's demand for additional Patriot air defence systems from the United States and its Western allies."The Russian air strikes on our country continue and air defense, specifically interceptors for Patriot systems against ballistic missiles, remains a top priority," Zelenskyy said in a post on Telegram on Friday.The Ukrainian president also said he had spoken with US vice president JD Vance after his meeting earlier this week in Washington with president Donald Trump.The renewed appeal comes amid uncertainty over future US military support. At the Nato summit in Ankara in July, president Trump said the United States would grant Ukraine a licence to manufacture Patriot systems. However, during a Cabinet meeting at the presidential retreat at Camp David on Friday, Trump indicated that no final decision had yet been taken on the proposal.Meanwhile, a fire broke out at St Basil's Cathedral on Moscow's Red Square early Saturday before being brought under control, according to Russia's state-run TASS news agency.TASS, citing operational services, said the blaze started in the director's office on the first floor."On the first floor, in the director's office, personal belongings and furniture caught fire. The area of the fire was around 10 sq. metres," a source told the agency, as reported by Kyiv Post.The cause of the fire was not immediately known. No injuries were reported. Around 10 fire engines were deployed to the site before operational services confirmed that the fire had been extinguished, TASS said.
Article Summary: Russia launches barrage of ballistic missiles and drones targeting Ukraine's capital Kyiv. Attack damages residential buildings, sparks multiple fires and leaves people trapped under debris. Ukrainian president reiterates demand for additional Patriot air defence systems from the United States. Fire breaks out at Moscow's St Basil's Cathedral.

Article Title: Reeling from powerful earthquake that killed 34, Japan hit with 5.7 magnitude quake 5 days later
Article Text:
5.7-magnitude quake hits Northern Japan days after powerful tremor

This is a developing story

A 5.7-magnitude earthquake jolted Japan's northern Hokkaido region on Saturday, just days after a powerful 7.1 magnitude earthquake struck southwestern Japan.The 7.1-magnitude quake caused widespread destruction, triggering an explosion at a shopping mall, toppling a factory chimney and flattening homes in the city of Yatsushiro, while also leaving roads cracked and buildings damaged. The death toll from the quake rose to 34 by Friday.
Article Summary: A 5.7-magnitude earthquake jolted Japan's northern Hokkaido region on Saturday, just days after a powerful 7.1 magnitude earthquake struck southwestern Japan. The death toll from the quake rose to 34 by Friday.

Article Title: Broad Peak avalanche: Three of 10 missing climbers found dead in PoK
Article Text:
Broad Peak avalanche leaves three dead

Rescuers searching for 10 climbers missing after an avalanche on PoK's Broad Peak recovered three bodies on Friday after locating four victims, as harsh weather and poor flying conditions hampered helicopter search-and-rescue operations.The Gilgit-Baltistan regional government identified the three recovered bodies as Nepali climber Pur Bahadur Gurung, Omani climber Nathira Ahmed, and American climber Mallory Geis. Authorities said the bodies were transported to a hospital for further procedures, as cited by AP.Adverse weather continued to hamper rescue operations on Friday, with poor flying conditions limiting search efforts, Gilgit-Baltistan chief minister Amjad Hussain said in a statement.The announcement came hours after officials said search teams had located the bodies of four climbers, though the identity of the fourth victim has not yet been confirmed. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity as they were not authorised to brief the media.According to Karrar Haidri, vice president of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, the climbers lost contact with their base camp after an avalanche struck Broad Peak while they were attempting to scale the mountain.“The team has been out of communication since Thursday,” said Haidri, adding that Pakistan Army helicopters were assisting in the search-and-rescue operation.The expedition included five Nepali climbers, along with climbers from Oman, the United States, Pakistan, China, and another foreign national. The Pakistani climber was identified as Sohail Sakhi, while the Chinese climber was identified only by the surname Wang.China said it was working to verify whether any of its nationals were among the 10 climbers reported missing.The expedition was led by renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja , a Nepal-born former British Army soldier widely known as Nims Dai. Purja gained global recognition after climbing the world's 14 highest peaks in a record 189 days in 2019, a feat documented in the Netflix film 14 Peaks: Nothing is Impossible. His record was later surpassed in 2023.Pakistan-based adventure company Moving Mountains said last month that the team had begun its journey to the town of Askole before attempting to summit Broad Peak, wishing the climbers a safe expedition.According to the company's website, the climb marked Mallory Geis' first attempt at an 8,000-metre peak in Pakistan. For Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, a guide with the company, as well as a geographer and high-altitude photographer who had scaled several of the world's highest mountains, it was expected to be his final expedition to an 8,000-metre peak.Geis, 39, who lived in San Antonio, had announced on social media earlier this year that she was closing her Pilates studio to pursue mountaineering full time, writing that she was taking “a giant leap of faith into the unknown to see where life goes. I have a sneaking suspicion there will be lots of helmets, harnesses, and crampons involved.”At 8,047 metres (26,401 feet), Broad Peak is the world's 12th-highest mountain. It is located in PoK's Karakoram range, which is home to five of the world's 14 peaks above 8,000 metres and attracts mountaineers from across the globe.Mountaineering accidents are not uncommon in northern Pakistan, where climbers frequently contend with avalanches, harsh terrain and rapidly changing weather conditions.
Article Summary: Search teams have recovered the bodies of three of the 10 climbers missing after an avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak. The bodies have been identified as Nepali climber Pur Bahadur Gurung, Omani climber Nathira Ahmed, and American climber Mallory Geis. The identity of the fourth victim has not been confirmed.

Article Title: US, Israel weigh bombarding Iran's energy infrastructure through the weekend: Report
Article Text:
US, Israel eye weekend bombing campaign on Iran's energy sites

The United States and Israel are planning a potential bombing campaign targeting Iran's energy infrastructure, with strikes possibly taking place over the weekend, CBS News reported on Friday, citing sources.However, US president Donald Trump has not yet given final approval for the operation.According to multiple US sources, officials have discussed wrapping up the operation before financial markets open on Monday amid concerns over the potential impact of the strikes on the US and global economy.However, no firm timeline has been finalised.The sources added that Israeli officials have been informed of the plans and are coordinating closely with the United States.A joint operation would mark Israel's return to active military operations after it paused its campaign during the US-brokered truce.Iran, meanwhile, has not launched attacks against Israel since the memorandum of understanding collapsed and the United States resumed combat operations in early July."Israel is unaware of a decision to restart full military operations, nor has been requested of Israel to join any military actions against Iran," an Israeli official was quoted as saying by CBS News.The development comes as Trump warned on Friday that Iran could be hit "very hard.""We'll be hitting him very hard and, you know, at some point they're going to say, 'We just can't take it anymore'," the US president said.The Wall Street Journal also reported that Trump had ordered preparations for a fresh military offensive aimed at pressuring Tehran into surrender, with the operation potentially beginning as early as this weekend.More than five months after the conflict began on February 28, when the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, the fighting shows no sign of easing, with both sides continuing to exchange attacks.Throughout the conflict, Trump has repeatedly threatened to target Iran's critical infrastructure. Last week, he warned that the United States would destroy a bridge or power plant each time commercial shipping in the strategically important Strait of Hormuz came under attack.The latest report also comes days after Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu met Trump and US defence secretary Pete Hegseth in Washington.
Article Summary: US, Israel eye weekend bombing campaign on Iran's energy sites, sources say. US president Donald Trump has not yet given final approval for the operation. Israeli officials have been informed of the plans and are coordinating closely with the United States. A joint operation would mark Israel's return to active military operations.

Article Title: Over 24,000 unaccompanied migrant children in the US risk losing legal aid as federal contract expires, nonprofits warn of deportation crisis
Article Text:
Over 24,000 unaccompanied migrant children in the US risk losing legal aid as federal contract expires, nonprofits warn of deportation crisis

Nonprofits warn children will lose critical legal support

Some organisations forced to shut programmes

Legal battle over funding continues

Advocates warn of consequences

More than 24,000 unaccompanied immigrant children facing deportation in the United States could lose access to legal representation after a federal contract funding nonprofit legal services expired on Friday, prompting warnings that thousands of vulnerable minors may be forced to navigate complex immigration proceedings alone.The contract's expiration affects about 90 nonprofit organisations across the country that provide legal assistance to children who entered the US without a parent or legal guardian.The crisis has been exacerbated by the Trump administration's refusal to reimburse legal service providers approximately $65 million for work they say has already been completed under the federal programme.According to Los Angeles Times, Lindsay Toczylowski, chief executive officer and co-founder of the Immigrant Defenders Law Center, said more than 1,500 unaccompanied children represented by her organisation in the Greater Los Angeles area could be affected.Other Los Angeles-based organisations expected to feel the impact include Public Counsel, the Central American Resource Center and the Immigration Center for Women and Children."I'm thinking of clients I personally have represented over the years — trafficking victims, asylum seekers, children separated from their parents — and wondering what chance kids like them will have if no one is there to fight for them," Toczylowski said.She added that lawyers often uncover abuse, document unlawful detention conditions and ensure children's legal rights are protected.Several nonprofit groups say they can no longer afford to continue representing unaccompanied children without federal funding.Melissa Lopez, whose nonprofit Estrella El Paso serves west Texas and New Mexico, said the government owes her organisation nearly $1 million."We are not able to sustain this program without this contract," Lopez said, adding that staff members working on the programme would have to be laid off after two decades of service.She described the region as a "legal desert," noting that there are already too few attorneys to meet community needs.In New York, Meena Shah, managing director of legal services at The Door, said her organisation is owed about $2 million and warned that expecting children to represent themselves in immigration court was unrealistic."It's preposterous to think that a child would be able to self-represent," Shah said.The dispute dates back to March 2025, when the US Department of Health and Human Services terminated its contract with the Acacia Center for Justice, which coordinates legal services through roughly 100 subcontracted organisations nationwide.A coalition of nonprofits subsequently filed a federal class-action lawsuit, arguing that ending the programme violated the William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008, which provides legal protections for unaccompanied migrant children.Although a federal judge in California ordered the administration in June 2025 to reinstate the contract, legal providers say the government later stopped paying invoices while demanding access to confidential client information, which they argue violates attorney-client privilege.A federal court hearing on the dispute is scheduled for August 6.Michael Lukens, executive director of the Amica Center for Immigrant Rights, accused the administration of undermining the legal aid programme by withholding payments."They are clearly trying to destroy the program by grinding down the financial health of nonprofits," Lukens said, warning that more layoffs and programme closures were likely if funding is not restored.Last month, Kids in Need of Defense announced it was ending its subcontract with the Acacia Center after accumulating more than $20 million in unpaid legal fees.Meanwhile, Democratic Representative Zoe Lofgren has reintroduced the Fair Day in Court for Kids Act, which would guarantee legal representation for unaccompanied children in immigration proceedings.Advocates argue the issue extends beyond immigration policy, saying legal representation is essential to ensuring due process and protecting children from exploitation."When you take lawyers away from children, you do not just take away legal representation," Toczylowski said. "You remove one of the few meaningful checks on government misconduct."
Article Summary: More than 24,000 unaccompanied immigrant children facing deportation in the US could lose access to legal representation. Federal contract funding nonprofit legal services expired on Friday, prompting warnings that vulnerable minors may be forced to navigate complex immigration proceedings alone. Trump administration's refusal to reimburse legal service providers approximately $65 million for work they say has already been completed under the federal programme.

Article Title: Florida evangelist who says passengers have no choice but to listen to her sermons removed from flight; Alaska Airlines puts her on no-fly list
Article Text:
Florida evangelist removed from flight after she started to preach.

Florida's preacher Whitney Lynn had to be deboarded from a San Diego-bound flight as she started addressing the passengers when there was a slight delay in the plane and called it 'God's perfect timing' to place their faith in Jesus. The incident took place on Thursday and now Alaska Airlines has put her on a no-fly list.Lynn posted the video on her social media and explained that no member of the cabin crew asked her to stop speaking. But an airline employee instructed her to leave, claiming that the flight crew no longer felt safe. In a statement, Alaska Airlines said the crew had become “increasingly concerned” about the passenger’s behaviour and removed her “for safety reasons.” The airline also confirmed that she has been prohibited from travelling on Alaska Airlines for the foreseeable future. Alaska Airlines’ sister carriers, Hawaiian Airlines and Horizon Air, also put her on a ban list as the incident is under review.Lynn said she was going to attend a funeral in California and found alternative travel."Maybe he’s sparing us from danger today," she said during the sermon, which lasted less than a minute.She was already in her seat when she was escorted out. Lynn repeatedly asked why she was being removed and described the incident as ‘spiritual warfare.’"Demons don't like the name of Jesus," she said as she was leaving. "We are in the last days. We are being persecuted, persecuted to be a Christian," she said. "I didn’t know the message of Jesus Christ was unsafe," she said. ‘So freedom of speech is not safe?’Lynn continued preaching after leaving the plane and claimed that she managed to convert two people.She told The Washington Post earlier that she preached on most flights and recorded the sermons for social media. "They have no choice but to hear the truth," she said of her fellow passengers. "When I have a gift and I have a life raft, if you’re drowning, I want to give you that life raft so you can be saved."
Article Summary: Whitney Lynn was on a San Diego-bound flight when she started preaching. Alaska Airlines said the crew had become ‘increasingly concerned’ about the passenger’s behaviour and removed her ‘for safety reasons’ The airline also confirmed that she has been prohibited from travelling on Alaska Airlines for the foreseeable future.

Article Title: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani denied chance to speak at funeral of soldier killed in Iranian attack: Report
Article Text:
NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

Prepared remarks released instead

Soldier killed in Iran missile attack

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani was reportedly not allowed to deliver a eulogy at the funeral of Army Sgt. Angel Sarah Rampersad in Queens on Friday, with multiple sources claiming the soldier's family chose to leave him off the list of speakers.According to the New York Post, Mamdani was seated in the fourth row during the funeral service in Ozone Park and was seen reviewing prepared remarks on an iPad as New York Governor Kathy Hochul and other dignitaries addressed mourners.The report, citing unnamed sources, said the mayor's name was never called, after which he appeared frustrated and put away his tablet.The report said Rampersad's family, described by sources as supporters of US President Donald Trump, allegedly did not want Mamdani to speak because they wished to avoid "political distractions."The report said the decision was linked to Mamdani's political positions, with sources claiming Rampersad's family wanted to avoid political distractions during the service. City Hall did not comment on the matter.Instead of delivering the eulogy, Mamdani's office later released his prepared remarks, in which he paid tribute to the 28-year-old soldier's sacrifice."It is often said that our fallen 'gave their tomorrows for our today,'" the prepared speech read."Sergeant Rampersad had tomorrows waiting for her... But she gave every one of them up so that we could have ours."Governor Kathy Hochul was among those who spoke during the service, along with local elected representatives and community leaders.Rampersad, 28, was among three US soldiers killed on July 17 during an Iranian missile attack on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan. A native of Ozone Park, she graduated from John Jay College of Criminal Justice before joining the US Army.Hundreds of mourners, including family members, fellow soldiers and local residents, attended the funeral at Calvary Assembly of God church. Following the service, NYPD officers escorted her coffin in a police procession to her final resting place on Long Island.
Article Summary: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani was reportedly not allowed to deliver a eulogy at the funeral of Army Sgt. Angel Sarah Rampersad in Queens on Friday. Multiple sources claimed the soldier's family chose to leave him off the list of speakers. The report said the family wanted to avoid "political distractions" during the service.

Article Title: Green Card updates for August: EB-1 may become unavailable for Indians
Article Text:
Green Card update for August

EB-1:

EB-2:

EB-3:

EB-4:

EB-5:

Family-sponsored Green Card

The US Department of State has already notified the changes that are going to happen to Green Card applicants this month as the fiscal year enters its final two months. The department also warned they might have to retrogress some dates and some Green Card categories may become unavailable because of the year-end adjustments. FY 2026 ends on September 30. If allotted number of Green Cards are exhausted before that, the department will make those visas unavailable until September 30.The EB1 category remained current for all countries except China and India. China advanced to July 1, 2023, while India remained at October 15, 2022.The EB2 category for India remains unavailable because all available visa numbers for FY2026 have been allocated. China remained at September 1, 2021, while the category remained current for all other countries.The EB3 category advanced by one month to Sep 1 2024, for all chargeability areas except those specifically listed. The category for Mexico likewise advanced one month to September 1, 2024. China advanced from December 22, 2021 to January 1, 2022. India and the Philippines remained unchanged at Jan 1, 2014, and August 1, 2023, respectively.The EB4 and Certain Religious Worker categories advanced by one month to October 15, 2022, for all countries.The EB5 Unreserved category remained current for most countries. However, the category continues to be unavailable for India and remains at December 1, 2016, for China. The EB5 set-aside categories (Rural, High Unemployment, and Infrastructure) remained current for all countries."High demand and number use by aliens chargeable to India in the EB-1 visa category may necessitate making the category unavailable in the coming weeks if India’s pro-rated limit in the EB-1 category is reached before the fiscal year ends. This situation will be continually monitored, and any necessary adjustments will be made accordingly," the latest update said."Sufficient demand and increased number use in the EB-2 visa category may make it necessary to retrogress the final action date or make the category unavailable in the coming months to hold number use within the maximum allowed under the FY 2026 annual limit," it said.In the F2A category, the final action date advanced to Jul 22, 2026, for all countries except Mexico, which advanced to Jul 22, 2025. In the F2B category, the final action date advanced to January 1, 2018, for all countries except Mexico and the Philippines. Mexico remained unchanged at Feb 15, 2009, while the Philippines advanced to Jun 1, 2013.
Article Summary: The US Department of State has already notified the changes that are going to happen to Green Card applicants this month. The department also warned they might have to retrogress some dates and some Green Card categories may become unavailable because of the year-end adjustments. FY 2026 ends on September 30.

Article Title: 'Prepare to depart': US embassies issue alert across Middle East amid Iran tensions
Article Text:
File photo: Middle East security situation

US warns of escalating security risks

Specific warnings for Jordan and Israel

Advisory follows Trump's fresh warning to Iran

Iran warns countries against supporting US

Shipping and regional tensions remain high

Wider conflict continues across the region

US embassies across several Middle Eastern countries on Saturday urged American citizens to consider leaving the region or be prepared to depart at short notice, warning of the possibility of an "unforeseen escalation" in the conflict involving Iran.The security alert was issued by US embassies in Bahrain, Iraq, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, a day after US President Donald Trump threatened to hit Iran "very hard".The advisory comes as the conflict between the United States and Iran continues to intensify, with repeated military exchanges disrupting travel, trade and security across the region.The identical security alerts described the situation in the Middle East as "fluid" and warned that the Iranian regime remained "unpredictable", citing recent attacks carried out "without warning or provocations" and the expansion of strikes to areas not previously targeted, including Egypt."Americans in the region should consider departing, or be prepared to depart should there be escalation," the advisory said.The embassies also advised US citizens to exercise "heightened vigilance" and prepare for possible flight cancellations, temporary airspace closures and wider travel disruptions.The advisory urged travellers to closely monitor airline operations and local safety guidance, while Americans planning trips to the region were asked to "seriously reconsider" their travel plans, as reported by PTI.The alert also warned that US diplomatic facilities, businesses and institutions worldwide could be targeted by Iran or groups aligned with Tehran."Americans should remain vigilant, as merely because US interests or businesses have not been attacked in a country in the past does not ensure their safety," the advisory said.The advisory contained country-specific guidance for some US nationals.Americans in Jordan were advised not to visit US military bases, which have recently come under Iranian missile attacks.In Israel, US citizens were urged to identify the nearest bomb shelter and remain prepared in case of fresh attacks.The US Embassy in Beirut also said it remained under "ordered departure status", meaning non-emergency US government personnel continue to remain relocated outside Lebanon.The travel warning came a day after Trump threatened further military action against Iran.Speaking during a Cabinet meeting at Camp David on Friday, Trump said the US would continue hitting Iran "very hard" until it "can't take it anymore".Later, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt accused Tehran of violating a previous truce understanding, saying Iran had resumed attacks on commercial shipping and American forces."President Trump is not going to stand by and allow this terrorist behavior to occur," Leavitt said.The latest advisory marks one of the broadest security alerts issued by Washington since the conflict intensified.Iran responded sharply to the US warnings and military posture.According to news agency AFP, Ali Abdollahi, head of Iran's military central command, accused Washington of escalating tensions and warned countries supporting the United States."Any country serving as defensive shield for criminal and aggressive America will be engulfed by the flames of war," he said in a statement carried by Iranian state television.Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Iran's Supreme Leader, also warned against attacks on Iranian infrastructure."You calculate through military equations, but we respond with the logic of history," he wrote on X, adding that attacking Iran's infrastructure would awaken "the fault lines" underpinning America's global influence.The security warning comes amid continued disruption to maritime traffic in the Gulf.An "unknown projectile" struck a tanker off the coast of Oman on Saturday, while British maritime authorities also reported another explosion near a separate vessel in the Strait of Hormuz.Kuwait's military also responded to a fresh round of Iranian drone attacks targeting vital facilities, although no casualties were reported.Maritime analytics firm Kpler said traffic through the Strait of Hormuz had dropped sharply as shipping companies reassessed risks."With US and Iranian public positions still at odds, operators are closely monitoring traffic volumes, routing behaviour and any diplomatic developments that could reshape risk across regional shipping lanes in the days ahead," Kpler said.Iran has tightened its control over navigation through the Strait of Hormuz since the conflict began, requiring vessels to obtain permission before transiting the strategic waterway.The latest developments come as the broader regional conflict shows little sign of easing.Israel carried out fresh strikes in Gaza after Hamas agreed to disarm under a US-backed phased peace framework, while Israeli forces also said they killed three Hezbollah fighters in southern Lebanon.One Israeli soldier was moderately injured during a close-quarters encounter with Hezbollah militants.The United States and Iran have remained engaged in hostilities since February, with repeated missile, drone and naval attacks continuing despite earlier ceasefire efforts.The prolonged conflict has disrupted regional economies, affected global energy markets and raised concerns over further escalation across the Middle East.
Article Summary: US embassies across several Middle Eastern countries issue security alert. Warn of possibility of an "unforeseen escalation" in conflict involving Iran. Warning comes a day after US President Donald Trump threatened to hit Iran "very hard" Warning comes amid continued disruption to maritime traffic in the Gulf.

Article Title: Trumpiana: Tryst with twistory!
Article Text:
As America slept, the POTUS retired to his throne room to unleash a bizarre blitz of AI slop portraying himself and Uncle Sam as the 'Guardians of the World.'

(By arrangement with

)

Not so long ago, Donald Trump made a twist with history, and now comes a second chance to rewrite the American story and warn gullible innocent citizens about all the ‘inaccurate information’ floating around.So as America slept, the POTUS retired to his throne room to unleash a bizarre blitz of AI slop portraying himself and Uncle Sam as the “Guardians of the World.”One movie-style poster depicted him as some kind of space hero called the “Cosmic Commander.” And in another, “A TIME TRAVEL EPIC,” he was pulling George Washington atop Mount Rushmore with Lincoln’s face missing — perhaps to make place for himself. “THE PAST WAS ABOUT TO CHANGE; HISTORY WAS ABOUT TO BE SAVED,” read the caption.The meme blitz came just after he ordered the installation of warning signs outside the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History cautioning visitors that it does not accurately reflect American history.The signage along sidewalks and walkways leading to the museum would tell visitors about the White House report, “Saving America’s Story,” accusing Smithsonian leadership of shifting “to extreme political activism rooted in Marxism, dividing and discouraging Americans.”Such signs are needed, the White House suggested as “in the last decade, Americans have witnessed a concerted effort to rewrite our history and force a factually baseless ideology that discredits American heroes.”Earlier, faced with a rapidly depleting arsenal, as jittery aides prevailed upon the commander-in-chief to hold back what a newspaper called the world’s heaviest hammer in waging peace in his Iran ‘excursion,’ he nevertheless declared victory on Truth Social.Trump posted a picture of himself leading spooky red-eyed soldiers in the mist, another of him steering a commandeered ship in the Persian Gulf, and yet another holding an American flag and attacking an Iranian boat.That was before the five-month long ‘excursion’ threatened to escalate into a conflagration with the U.S. and Iran firing barrages of missiles at each other and strikes spreading to Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Tehran digging in for “either all or nothing” despite Trump’s warning that it was “going to get a beating.”With the war going on forever, an anonymous group of artists called the Secret Handshake which had previously installed a 10-foot-tall “Iran War Participation Trophy” mocking Trump in Washington DC, took the statue for display in New York City.Meanwhile, with the American economy slowing down amid an unpopular war causing an affordability crisis, Trump flew to Michigan to watch luxury cars race and blame his predecessor Joe Biden for the rising prices.Addressing workers at a General Motors facility in Michigan, he disclosed that the White House had just ordered 250 brand new Cadillac Escalades, giant SUVs with a retail price of more than $90,000 each sans customization for security.“We ordered 250 Escalades. That’s how we look sharp in those cavalcades, you know,” Trump beamed. “We look sharp in those Escalades. Our guys are very spoiled. They’re very spoiled. They like the Escalade. So do I.”And as his team curiously missed the deadline to request a rehearing of the Supreme Court case that knocked down Trump’s order ending birthright citizenship, a law that makes anyone born on U.S. soil a citizen — he piled on the apex court.“Does anybody have any idea how much Money and Prestige the United States Supreme Court has cost our Nation with their negative Rulings on Birthright Citizenship and TARIFFS?” he asked with “The answer, TRILLIONS AND TRILLIONS OF DOLLARS!”But a Wisconsin brewery whose owner once promised to give away free beer if Trump dies is set to lose its alcohol permit Aug. 4 for allegedly transporting canned beer from Illinois without the required permits and taxes.Revocation of the permit comes about three months after FBI agents grilled the brewery owner Kirk Bangstad over a Facebook post apparently referring to an alleged assassination attempt against Trump following the White House Correspondents’ abandoned dinner on April 25.“Well, we almost got #freebeerday. Either a brother or sister in the Resistance needs to work on their marksmanship or he faked another assassination to get a positive news cycle,” Bangstad wrote from the brewery’s account.Meanwhile, construction of Trump’s $400 million 90,000-square-foot big beautiful ballroom and bunker complex to make way for which he demolished the historic East Wing, is racing ahead despite unresolved legal challenges with a federal judge barring construction over ground.And the State Department announced it will be offering more passports bearing Trump’s picture due to “overwhelming demand.” The design was introduced to commemorate America’s 250th anniversary on July 4, with plans to produce it in limited quantities.The builder-in-chief himself was excited to announce a massive, $22.5 billion overhaul of Dulles International Airport, the capital’s air travel hub with direct flights to more than 50 countries.“This is very exciting to me as a builder — somebody that builds lots of big, nice projects before I got here, and we’re doing some of the best in the world right now,” Trump said in the Oval Office, seated before a large model of the newly imagined airport that covered his desk.The “HISTORIC investment for a landmark transformation” calls for new terminals, gold decor and an end to the airport’s iconic “mobile lounges” known as “people movers.” Trump, who called Dulles “a terrible place to be,” is said to have personally edited the plans.“You know, it’s a great thrill,” Trump said when asked why he’s so focused on making Washington beautiful again, “Whether you’re a Republican or Democrat, you don’t want to go and be subjected to this airport.”If Trump is still around for his third or fourth term when the new improved airport gets ready in eight to 10 years, it would in all certainty be renamed “DJT” — Greeting visitors with a sign: ‘Welcome to 1984!’ Just kidding.
Article Summary: As America slept, the POTUS retired to his throne room to unleash a bizarre blitz of AI slop portraying himself and Uncle Sam as the ‘Guardians of the World’ One movie-style poster depicted him as some kind of space hero called the “Cosmic Commander.” And in another, “A TIME TRAVEL EPIC,” he was pulling George Washington atop Mount Rushmore with Lincoln’s face missing — perhaps to make place for himself.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos' ex-wife MacKenzie Scott: “There are lots of resources each of us can pull from our safes to share with others…”
Article Text:
Quote of the day by MacKenzie Scott



“There are lots of resources each of us can pull from our safes to share with others. And something greater rises up every time we give.”

Understanding the meaning of the quote



The hidden strength behind generosity



About MacKenzie Scott



Lessons from the quote



Why the message still matters



A common misunderstanding



Generosity is often discussed in terms of money, yet most people recognise that the moments which stay with them rarely depend on financial value alone. A thoughtful conversation, practical help during a difficult week, a useful introduction or simply making time for someone can leave a lasting impression. Giving has always taken many forms, even if public attention tends to focus on charitable donations and large fundraising campaigns. This quote from MacKenzie Scott points in a different direction. It suggests that every individual has something worth offering and that generosity changes not only the person receiving help but also the person who chooses to give. The idea is simple, though its implications reach much further than they first appear.MacKenzie Scott uses the word "resources" in a broad sense. She is not limiting it to wealth or possessions. Skills, experience, encouragement, patience, knowledge and attention all have value, and many of them cost little or nothing to share.The reference to "our safes" is also interesting because it suggests that people often keep valuable things protected or unused. Sometimes that is money, but it can just as easily be confidence, creativity or opportunities that could benefit someone else.The quote asks readers to think about what they already possess rather than what they lack.The second sentence shifts the focus away from the recipient. Scott argues that giving creates something new within the giver as well. Kindness can strengthen relationships, build trust and encourage a stronger sense of purpose. In that sense, generosity is not simply a transfer from one person to another. It becomes an experience that affects both sides.It frames it as an action that expands rather than diminishes what people have. That is an important distinction. Many people hesitate to give because they assume it leaves them with less, whether that means less time, less money or fewer opportunities.Life often suggests the opposite. Sharing knowledge at work can improve an entire team without reducing the person's own expertise. Helping a neighbour may strengthen a community that later offers support in return. Mentoring someone does not erase years of experience; it allows that experience to continue through someone else's progress.There is also a quieter message within the quote. People sometimes underestimate the value of what they can contribute because they compare themselves with those who possess more. Scott shifts attention away from comparison and towards participation. Every person has access to something that may be useful to someone else.MacKenzie Scott is an American novelist and one of the world's most prominent philanthropists. Before becoming widely known for her charitable work, she published novels recognised for their literary style and careful character development.In recent years, Scott has reshaped public conversations about philanthropy through an approach that differs from traditional large-scale charitable giving. Rather than attaching lengthy conditions to many donations, she has directed substantial unrestricted grants to charities, educational institutions and community organisations, allowing them greater freedom to decide how the funds should be used. Her approach has drawn attention because it places trust in local leaders and organisations that understand their communities' needs.The first lesson is that generosity is broader than charity. Many people can offer guidance, encouragement or practical support even when financial giving is not possible.Another lesson concerns perspective. People frequently focus on what they hope to gain, while overlooking the abilities and opportunities they already possess. The quote encourages an inventory of existing strengths instead of waiting for ideal circumstances.It also reminds readers that generosity is often cumulative. Small actions repeated over time may have greater long-term influence than occasional dramatic gestures. A teacher who consistently supports students, a colleague who shares expertise or a volunteer who gives a few hours each month can shape lives without attracting much attention.Finally, the quote suggests that giving is connected with personal growth. It invites people to see generosity not as an obligation but as a way of developing empathy, confidence and stronger relationships.In today’s world, success can be measured by how much one accumulates. While careers, possessions, accomplishments, and other personal successes are highlighted more than any act of generosity, social media may add to the perception that only things that are seen have value.This being said, the quotation provides an alternative measure of value. Communities still rely on many volunteers, mentors, caregivers, teachers, neighbours, and many other people who work hard but never get mentioned. These people earn their influence through constant sharing of whatever they have.At the same time, the quotation seems to fit the world of business and corporate culture. More and more companies realise that teamwork requires people who are willing to share knowledge rather than keep it for themselves. In many cases, teamwork works well if members see that sharing is more important than competing.A common misconception regarding the quote is that it is meant for wealthy people since MacKenzie Scott is well known for donating large sums of money in charity work. This is a mistaken view of the quote.The vocabulary used intentionally goes past giving money. It focuses on giving resources and not wealth. Resources that can take the form of time, patience, encouragement, experience, imagination or even opportunities that cannot be quantified in financial terms.In that context, it means that the quote is not necessarily about performing an act of charity but about simple actions that everyone is capable of doing irrespective of their economic standing.
Article Summary: MacKenzie Scott is an American novelist and one of the world's most prominent philanthropists. The quote asks readers to think about what they already possess rather than what they lack. People sometimes underestimate the value of what they can contribute because they compare themselves with those who possess more.

Article Title: Trump rejects Iran role in Minnesota water cyberattacks, blames 'grossly incompetent' Tim Walz
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump

Walz says Trump knows who is behind attacks

Dozens of water systems targeted

Federal agencies probe Iran link

US President Donald Trump on Friday rejected claims that Iran was behind a series of cyberattacks targeting Minnesota's water systems, instead blaming the state's Democratic leadership without providing evidence.Speaking during a Cabinet meeting at Camp David, Trump said reports linking the attacks to Iran were unconvincing."We heard in Minnesota there was a cyberattack and they blame it on Iran. I don't think so. I blame Minnesota because they're grossly incompetent," Trump was quoted as saying by news agency Reuters. He also described Governor Tim Walz as "corrupt."His remarks came even as US investigators continue examining whether the attacks were carried out by Iran or hackers linked to Tehran. Officials have stressed that the assessment remains preliminary and could change as the investigation progresses.Governor Tim Walz rejected Trump's comments, saying the president was ignoring intelligence assessments and politicising a national security issue."Trump knows exactly who is responsible for this attack, and knows that other states were hit too. This is what modern warfare looks like," Walz said in a post on X.Walz also argued that staffing cuts to the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) under the now-defunct Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) had weakened the country's cyber defences."DOGE took an axe to CISA and left the US exposed to cyberattacks. Thankfully, our experts in Minnesota were able to identify the vulnerability quickly and work with local communities to stop it," he said.Minnesota IT Services (MNIT) said more than 30 community water systems were targeted on July 26 and 27 in what it described as a coordinated cyberattack.According to state officials, attackers remotely accessed internet-connected equipment used to monitor and control water infrastructure, including programmable logic controllers (PLCs). In several cases, passwords and IP addresses were altered, disrupting operators' ability to monitor systems.Authorities said there is no evidence of ongoing disruption to drinking water services, and no communities have been asked to change their water usage.Federal investigators have briefed state officials on the possibility that Iran or Iran-linked hackers could be responsible for the attacks, although no formal attribution has been made.The FBI and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) have warned that similar incidents have been reported in at least seven US states, with some attacks affecting water operations. Georgia and Michigan are among the states that have reported comparable activity.CISA has also warned of an increase in cyber campaigns targeting water and wastewater facilities, saying attackers have been exploiting internet-connected industrial control systems to lock operators out of critical equipment.Cybersecurity experts have noted that the tactics used in the Minnesota incidents resemble methods previously associated with Iranian-affiliated hacking groups, though investigators say the inquiry remains ongoing.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump rejects claims that Iran was behind a series of cyberattacks targeting Minnesota's water systems. He instead blames the state's Democratic leadership without providing evidence. Governor Tim Walz rejected Trump's comments, saying the president was ignoring intelligence assessments and politicising a national security issue.

Article Title: Savannah Guthrie begs public after mother's disappearance; ransom note said 'buried in nature'
Article Text:
FILE - A collection of yellow flowers and notes sit at the home of Nancy Guthrie, the missing mother of "Today" show host Savannah Guthrie

Today show host, Savannah Guthrie, has made a fresh appeal for information about her mother who disappeared from her Arizona home. She urged anyone who recognises the writing in two ransom notes released by authorities to come forward, saying her family is “desperate” for answers.Guthrie’s mother, Nancy Guthrie, disappeared from her home outside Tucson on February 1, after spending the previous evening with her family. Investigators have said they believe she was taken against her will. No arrests have been made in the case.In an Instagram post on Saturday, Guthrie said her family was “desperate” and “begging for help”, urging anyone with information about her mother’s disappearance to come forward.She also drew attention to two ransom notes that authorities released a day earlier, asking the public to pay particular attention to the writing style and unusual word choices in the messages. Investigators believe the notes contain distinctive patterns of syntax and phrasing that could be recognised by someone who knows or has interacted with their writer.“Someone knows something. Someone suspects something. Someone recognises the writing in the ransom demand notes,” Guthrie wrote, according to the Associated Press.She also appealed to anyone who may have noticed a friend, relative or acquaintance behaving unusually since Nancy disappeared — including someone who suddenly changed their appearance, left the Tucson area or developed an unusual interest in the case.Authorities released two notes on Friday that were sent to a Tucson television station shortly after Guthrie vanished. The first note, sent on February 2, demanded $4 million in cryptocurrency and claimed Guthrie would be released unharmed if the ransom was paid. It also threatened her life if the demand was not met.A second note, sent four days later, claimed Guthrie had died shortly after being kidnapped and said her remains had been buried “in nature”. Authorities have not publicly established who wrote the notes or confirmed whether the claims about Guthrie’s death are true.Investigators have also released surveillance footage showing an unidentified man near Guthrie’s home. The FBI said the person appeared to tamper with her doorbell camera and was about 5 feet 9 inches to 10 inches tall with an average build.The FBI is offering $100,000 for information leading to Guthrie’s recovery or the arrest and conviction of someone involved in her disappearance. The Guthrie family has separately offered a $1 million reward.
Article Summary: Guthrie’s mother, Nancy Guthrie, disappeared from her home outside Tucson on February 1, after spending the previous evening with her family. Investigators have said they believe she was taken against her will. In an Instagram post on Saturday, Guthrie said her family was “desperate’ and “begging for help’, urging anyone with information to come forward.

Article Title: 'Returned to the US 3 days before visa expiry': Indian H-1B holder shares what happened next
Article Text:
An Indian H-1B worker entered US three days before visa expiry.

What happens now?

Amid much panic and apprehension over international and domestic travel for visa holders, an Indian H-1B employee shared the experience returning to the US three days before the expiry of the visa. The person said that the visa validity was until July 31 and the extension was filed in March under regular processing, which remained pending."I traveled to India on June 28 due to an emergency and returned to the US on July 28, just 3 days before my H-1B was set to expire, through Seattle Port of Entry," the visa holder said."The CBP officer asked for my new I-797 approval notice. I explained that my extension is still pending and showed the H-1B extension receipt notice. The officer verified the filing and asked when I planned to travel back to India for visa stamping if the new petition was approved. I replied that I would likely travel in December or June," the post read.The person was then taken for a secondary inspection, where the passport, phone and other documents were taken."Another officer then returned my documents and informed me that I was being admitted only until August 10, 2026.When I asked what that meant, I didn't receive any explanation. They simply asked me to proceed to my connecting flight," the post added.The post gained a lot of attention as immigration experts are advising visa holders to put off travel plans. Social media users said the H-1B visa holder must inform the employer's attorney immediately about the August 10 date. The visa holder also must upgrade to premium processing for the H-1B petition so that the extension plea is addressed faster before the current entry period lapses.CBP officers do not have the legal authority to grant a stay on a pending petition. Since the officer was admitting the person just three days before the visa expiry, they had to follow the due procedure and set the new date, giving a 10-day grace which is legally permitted.
Article Summary: An Indian H-1B employee shared the experience returning to the US three days before the expiry of the visa. The person said that the visa validity was until July 31 and the extension was filed in March under regular processing, which remained pending.

Article Title: Hospital staff plan wedding in just 24 hours as couple together for 15 years marry before bride undergoes life-changing brain tumour surgery
Article Text:
Hospital staff plan wedding in just 24 hours as couple together for 15 years marry before bride undergoes life-changing brain tumour surgery

Hospital staff organise wedding overnight

'There she is, my beautiful bride'

'Hope in the midst of uncertainty'
